<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par139 />supported by {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=42|verse=25}} and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=17|verse=17}}, it is inconceivable that such an inversion of {{GHGterm|nomen regens}} and ''rectum'' should occur. It is more likely, either that the second substantive is in apposition to {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ}} (thus {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=9|verse=5}} ''at the hand of every man, his brother'', [unless it is a combination of the two readings {{GHGheb|text=מִיַּד אִישׁ}} and {{GHGheb|text=מִיַּד הָֽאָדָם}}]; similarly 15:10 ''and he laid each'' or, more exactly, ''one piece of it'', &c., and so probably also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=17|verse=17}} ''every one'', sc. ''his name''), or {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ}} precedes as a kind of ''casus pendens'', and only receives its nearer definition from the following substantive with suffix; thus {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=41|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=42|verse=25|hidebook=1}} (according to the context = ''to every one in his sack''); 42:35, where {{GHGheb|text=צְרוֹר־כַּסְפּוֹ בְּשַׂקּוֹ}} is virtually the predicate of {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=12|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=28|verse=21|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=5|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=26|verse=54|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=23|verse=35}}, and especially {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=7|verse=10}}.<ref>Cf. on the whole question the thorough discussion by Budde, ''Die bibl. Urgeschichte'', p. 283 ff.: according to him, the words in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=9|verse=5}} are to be rendered ''at the hand of one another'' (from men mutually) ''will I require it''. [In support of this view, Budde points to {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=7|verse=10}} {{GHGheb|text=בִּלְבַבְכֶם וְרָעַת אִישׁ אָהִיו אַל־תַּהְשְׁבוּ}}, which in the light of 8:17, {{GHGheb|text=וְאִישׁ אֶת־רָעַת רֵעֵהוּ אַל־תַּחְשְׁבוּ בִּלְבַבְכֶם}}, can only, he observes, be rendered ‘and devise not ''the hurt of one another'' in your heart’. So also König, ''Syntax'', § 33.]</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|139|d}}
(''b'') ''Any one, some one'', e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=13|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=8|verse=7}}, with a negative ''no one'';<ref>Cf. also {{GHGheb|text=אֵין־אִישׁ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=39|verse=11}}. On the expression of the idea of ''no one'' by means of {{GHGheb|text=אֵין}} with a following participle, see the ''Negative Sentences'', {{GHGpar|152|l}}.</ref> so after {{GHGheb|text=אַל־}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=16|verse=19}}, 29; before {{GHGheb|text=לֹא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=23|verse=6}} and frequently.—Instead of {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ}} we sometimes find in a similar sense {{GHGheb|text=אָדָם|translate=man, homo}}, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=1|verse=2}} (cf. {{GHGheb|text=כְּאַחַד הָֽאָדָם|translate=as any one else}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=16|verse=7}}, 11), {{GHGheb|text=נֶ֫פֶשׁ}} (''soul'') ''person'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=2|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=5|verse=1|hidebook=1}}, &c., and in a neuter sense {{GHGheb|text=דָּבָר}} (prop. word, thing) for ''anything'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=18|verse=14}}, or {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־דָּבָר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=5|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=31|verse=23}}. With a negative {{GHGheb|text=דָּבָר}} means ''nothing''; thus after {{GHGheb|text=אַל־}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=8}}; after {{GHGheb|text=לֹא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=8|verse=5}}.—Cf. finally, {{GHGheb|text=מֵֽאַחַד|translate=any one}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=15|verse=7}}; ''anything'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=18|verse=10}} (but in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=4|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=5|verse=13|hidebook=1}} {{GHGheb|text=מֵֽאַחַת}}) and the expressions noticed in {{GHGpar|144|e}}. The latter include also instances like {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=18|verse=32}} ''I have no pleasure'' {{GHGheb|text=בְּמֹוֹת הַמֵּת|translate=in the death of him that dieth}}, i.e. ''of any man''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|139|e}}
(''c'') In connexion with {{GHGheb|text=אָחִיו|translate=his brother}} or {{GHGheb|text=רֵעֵ֫הוּ|translate=his neighbour}}, {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ|translate=one}}, masc. (as {{GHGheb|text=אִשָּׁה|translate=one}}, fem., in connexion with {{GHGheb|text=אֲחוֹתָהּ|translate=her sister}} or {{GHGheb|text=רְעוּתָהּ|translate=her neighbour}}) is used to represent the ideas of ''alter—alter, the one—the other''<ref>Elsewhere {{GHGheb|text=זֶה... זֶה}} are used in a similar sense, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=14|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=6|verse=3}}; also {{GHGheb|text=הָֽאֶחָד... הָֽאֶחָד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=14|verse=6}}, or the substantive is repeated, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=47|verse=21}} (''from one end... to the other end'').</ref> (in reference to persons, animals, or things without life; see the Lexicon) or the idea of ''one another'', e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=13|verse=11}} ''and they separated them selves'' {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ מֵעַל אָחִיו|translate=the one from the other}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=26|verse=3}} ''five curtains'' ({{GHGheb|text=יְרִיעֹת}} fem.) ''shall be coupled together'' {{GHGheb|text=אִשָּׁה אֶל־אֲחֹתָהּ|translate=one to another}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|139|f}}
2. {{GHGheb|text=נֶ֫פֶשׁ|translate=soul, person}} expresses the idea of ''self'',<ref>On the representation of this idea by pronouns, separate and suffixed, see {{GHGpar|135|a}}, i and k.</ref> both in the singular, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=19|verse=8}}, 16, 29:24, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=18|verse=4}} (in all cases {{GHGheb|text=נַפְשׁוֹ}} equivalent to ''himself'') and in the plural, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=37|verse=9}}, &c. Similar to this is the use of {{GHGheb|text=בְּקִרְבָּךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=18|verse=12}} (prop. ''in her inward part'') in the sense of ''within herself''.<ref>In a similar way the idea of ''self'' in Arabic, as in Sanskrit (''âtman''), is paraphrased by ''soul, spirit''; in Arabic also by ''eye''; in Rabbinic by {{GHGheb|text=גּוּף|translate=body}}, {{GHGheb|text=גֶּ֫רֶם}} or {{GHGheb|text=עֶ֫צֶם|translate=bone}}, in Ethiopic and Amharic by ''head'', in Egyptian by ''mouth, hand'', &c.; cf. also the Middle High German ''mîn lîp, dîn lîp'', for ''ich, du''. However, {{GHGheb|text=נֶ֫פֶשׁ}} in such cases is never (not even in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=46|verse=2}} {{GHGheb|text=נַפְשָׁם|translate=they themselves}}) a merely otiose periphrasis for the personal pronoun, but always involves a reference to the ''mental'' personality, as affected by the senses, desires, &c.</ref><section end=par139 /><noinclude>
